title: FAUST. IX. Multiband, multiscale dust study of L1527 IRS. Evidence for variations in dust properties within the envelope of a class 0/I young stellar object
question: Characterize the dust continuum emission, spectral index, and dust emissivity index across disk and envelope scales (10 to 10^3 au) in the class 0/I YSO L1527 IRS to test for variations in dust properties and early grain growth.

data.sensitivity: FAUST B3: 0.025 mJy, FAUST B6: 0.026 mJy; 12m: 0.03-0.3 mJy; 7m: 0.2-1.44 mJy

what.value: VLA flux density measurements of L1527 at 43.5, 22.5, 8.5, and 5 GHz (7.0, 13.3, 35.2, and 60 mm)

evidence.quote: To offer a more comprehensive view to the reader, we extended the range of wavelengths by including literature Very Large Array (VLA) measurements from (cite: Melis2011), up to 6 cm.

what.value: PdBI continuum visibility fluxes and dust emissivity index measurements of L1527 at 1.3 and 3.2 mm

evidence.loc: L1527 as seen in the visibility space
evidence.quote: Among other class 0/Is of the CALYPSO survey, the continuum emission of the envelope infalling on L1527 has been studied in (cite: Galametz2019), hereafter G19, who used PdBI observations at 1.3 and 3.2 millimeter.

what.value: Target properties in Table 1: age, protostellar mass, bolometric luminosity, and envelope mass

evidence.quote: The age of the object has been roughly estimated by [1] (cite: Tobin2012) based on the mass loss rate of the source. The mass of the protostar has been estimated by means of kinematical analysis by [1] and [2] (cite: Aso2017).

The bolometric luminosity was reported by [3] (cite: Karska2018) and might suffer up to a factor two uncertainty due to the high inclination of the disk (e.g., (cite: Whitney2003)).The envelope mass was derived in [4] (cite: Motte2001)

recipe.goal: Prepare, align, rescale, self-calibrate, and concatenate multi-epoch ALMA/ACA continuum visibilities
recipe.method: Split Band 3 into two frequency groups (88 and 100 GHz) to avoid frequency smearing; visually inspect cubes and flag spectral lines; channel-average spectral windows; fix visibility weights with statwt; image with tclean and fit Gaussian peak with imfit; shift phase center to peak with fixvis and align metadata coordinates with fixplanets; rescale fluxes across execution blocks in overlapping uv-ranges using gencal/applycal; perform 3 rounds of phase-only self-calibration (solint=inf, 60s, 10s); combine datasets with concat and cut at shortest common baseline of 9.8 klambda.

recipe.goal: Model visibilities to disentangle compact disk and extended envelope emission
recipe.method: Fit a 10-parameter composite geometrical model (Gaussian for the compact disk plus a Plummer-like broken power law for the envelope) to the visibilities at each of the 5 frequencies using galario.
key_parameters: 10 free parameters: I_0 (f_0), r, sigma, inc, PA, R_in, R_out, p, dRA, dDec
assumptions: Envelope emission is constant within R_i, follows Plummer power law between R_i and R_out, and is zero beyond R_out; compact disk is represented by a 2D Gaussian

recipe.goal: Construct and fit the circumstellar disk SED and estimate free-free contamination
recipe.method: Combine the ALMA disk flux densities derived from the Gaussian model component at 5 frequencies with literature VLA measurements from Melis et al. (2011) up to 6 cm, and fit power-law spectral indices across 0.88-7 mm and 35-60 mm.
key_parameters: Wavelength ranges fitted: 0.88-7 mm for dust disk SED, 35-60 mm for free-free slope

recipe.goal: Derive the envelope spectral index as a function of spatial scale and position angle
recipe.method: Subtract the best-fit galario Gaussian disk component from the visibilities, log-uniformly bin the residual envelope visibilities across uv-distance (starting from ~9 klambda), and perform a weighted linear regression to log10(F) vs log10(nu) across all 5 frequencies in each uv-bin, as well as in three position angle sectors (envelope, outflow, cavity walls) and between adjacent band pairs.
key_parameters: Flux calibration uncertainty: 10% for B7, 5% for B3, B4, B6
Angle sectors: envelope (-20 deg < PA < 20 deg), outflow (70 deg < PA < 110 deg), cavity walls (remaining zones)

recipe.goal: Compute temperature-corrected dust emissivity index beta(R) and fit its radial gradient
recipe.method: Check optical depth by comparing specific intensity F_0.88mm/Omega to Planck function B(T_dust) using a centrally illuminated envelope temperature profile; correct for departures from the Rayleigh-Jeans approximation by fitting log10[F_nu / B_nu(T)] = beta * log10(nu) + A in each uv-bin; fit a linear relation between beta and log10(R_au) using Bayesian linear regression in linmix.
key_parameters: Radial scale range fitted: 50 to 2000 au
assumptions: Dust temperature profile T(R) = 38 L^0.2 (R / 100 au)^-0.4 with L_bol = 1.6 L_sun and d = 140 pc
Envelope continuum emission is optically thin at all studied wavelengths and scales, and temperature profile is exact so Delta_beta = Delta_alpha

evidence.loc: L1527 as seen in the visibility space
evidence.quote: We also show that the associated spectral index lies in the range $1.5 < \alpha_{0.88-3.4mm} < 2.4$.
In particular, we find that the compact emission has a deprojected width of $0.15\ensuremath{''} < \sigma_{fit} < 0.28\ensuremath{''}$ on the sky, depending on the Band.

answer_key.quantity: Disk radius in Band 7 (2 sigma contour)

evidence.quote: If we define the radius of the disk to be the $2\sigma$ contour of the Gaussian component, then $R_{disk} \sim 75$ au in B7, consistent with what was found in the kinematical analysis of (cite: Aso2017).

answer_key.quantity: Disk flux density at 348 GHz (0.86 mm)
Disk flux density at 249 GHz (1.2 mm)
Disk flux density at 141 GHz (2.1 mm)
Disk flux density at 101 GHz (3.0 mm)
Disk flux density at 88 GHz (3.4 mm)

evidence.quote: Fitting the SED in the 0.88 to 7-millimeter range using our measurements along with the values of (cite: Melis2011), we find an optically thick disk with $\alpha = 2.1 \pm 0.1$.
The slope at these longer wavelengths is $\alpha_{35-60} = 0.33 \pm 0.17$, as reported in Fig. 5 and is compatible with what is expected for free-free emission (cite: Panagia1975).
Figure 6 shows that the fitted spectral index of the envelope of L1527 appears roughly flat in the studied range that spans from $\sim 2000$ down to 50 au, $\alpha \sim 3$.

answer_key.quantity: Envelope dust emissivity index range (50 to 2000 au)

evidence.quote: We find evidence for an outward increasing $\beta$, rising from 0.8 to 1.6 between 50 and 2000 au radial scales

answer_key.quantity: Slope of radial dust emissivity index gradient d(beta)/d(log10 R_au)

evidence.quote: $$\begin{equation} \beta(R_{au}) = 0.37^{+0.17}_{-0.16} \cdot \log_{10}( R_{au}) - 0.23^{+0.45}_{-0.46}. \label{eq:beta_grad} \end{equation}$$

answer_key.quantity: Intercept of radial dust emissivity index relation

evidence.quote: $$\begin{equation} \beta(R_{au}) = 0.37^{+0.17}_{-0.16} \cdot \log_{10}( R_{au}) - 0.23^{+0.45}_{-0.46}. \label{eq:beta_grad} \end{equation}$$

answer_key.quantity: Dust emissivity index at R = 300 au (and reported at 500 au)

evidence.quote: $$\begin{equation} \beta(R=300 au) = 1.15 \pm 0.08. \end{equation}$$
Secondly, G19 reported a fitted $\beta_{500 au} = 1.41 \pm 0.16$ while we find $\beta_{500 au} = 1.15 \pm 0.08$ based on Eq.[\[eq:beta\]](#eq:beta).

score_reason: All 20 ALMA project codes, execution dates, rescaling factors, CASA versions, self-calibration intervals, analytical equations, and best-fit parameter tables are provided. However, reproducing the exact visibility combination requires knowing the unstated line-free channel masks across ~48 execution blocks, the reference datasets for flux rescaling, and the exact uv-binning and MCMC prior bounds.
rediscovery_reason: All 20 ALMA/ACA datasets are public in the ALMA archive, the visibility-plane modeling uses standard open-source tools (CASA, galario, linmix), and the main results (disk fluxes across 5 frequencies, 10-parameter model fits, and the radial beta gradient) are concrete numeric benchmarks.
